label: TP-Link EAP225-Wall
description: AC1200 wall-plate access point: one 10/100 uplink (PoE in), two 10/100 downlink ports and a third 10/100 port with a 13 W PoE passthrough, dual-band Wi-Fi 5. The passthrough port is a PSE only while the uplink is fed 802.3at; on 802.3af the AP runs and the passthrough jack stays dead.
notes: Vendor figures from the TP-Link/Omada page for the UK model, https://www.omadanetworks.com/uk/business-networking/omada-wifi-wall-plate/eap225-wall/ (HTTP 200, 153,844 B, text/html, read 2026-11-21; www.tp-link.com/uk/... 301s here): Interface - "Uplink: 1x 10/100 Mbps Ethernet Port / Downlink: 3x 10/100 Mbps Ethernet Ports (One port supports PoE OUT. The PoE OUT feature requires 802.3at PoE+ input and the maximum output is 13 W.)"; Power Supply - "802.3af/802.3at PoE"; Max. Power Consumption - "9 watts /25.5 watts (PoE Out Included)". The US v2 page named in sourceUrl, https://www.tp-link.com/us/business-networking/omada-sdn-access-point/eap225-wall/v2/ (HTTP 200, 224,096 B, read 2026-11-21; the same v2 content is also served under the /omada-wifi-wall-plate/ shelf slug, 181,584 B), carries the same port census as "1 x 10/100Mbps with PoE pass-thru (requires 802.3at PoE+ power supply on PD port.)" but prints no output wattage - which is why the 13 W traces to the UK page. The two consumption rows are the check on that figure: 25.5 - 9 is 16.5 W, more than the 13 W the jack is allowed to pass, so 25.5 W is the 802.3at class-4 ceiling the box may draw rather than a measured sum, and the vendor's stated output - not the subtraction - is what is modelled. The UK page also marks the model "Product EOL : Replace with EAP235- Wall"; the successor is already catalogued at devices/tp-link/eap235-wall.json, whose passthrough is the same 13 W. The uplink keeps the 12.95 W 802.3af class-3 allowance because 9 W is what the AP alone draws; the box asks for the 802.3at class only once the passthrough is in use. The passthrough's 802.3at precondition is not expressible in the spec schema today - `poe.budgetW` is unconditional - which the poe note says outright. Radios are AC1200 (300M + 867M from the interface rows), the family class rather than a per-band row quoted on this page; the uplink being fast Ethernet while the radios are AC is the real planning constraint on this model.

poe.note: 13 W, the vendor's stated maximum output on the single passthrough port, quoted as "the maximum output is 13 W" (UK page, read 2026-11-21). One PSE port, so the device total is the port ceiling - and the condition is part of the figure: with an 802.3af uplink the passthrough supplies nothing at all, while the AP still powers up and draws 9 W. In use the box pulls 25.5 W including PoE Out, which is 802.3at class 4, so the upstream port feeding it must be PoE+ before this budget exists. The catalogue cannot yet say "this PSE exists only when the input is 802.3at", so a lab that feeds the AP from an 802.3af port will still see eth3 allocate 13 W: the condition is recorded here and in the description, and it wants a schema field before the engine can refuse it.
